title: ICSE CLASS 10 — Social Science | Resources Development Types

subject: icse10-sst

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an abiotic resource?

options.explanation: Forests are biotic resources, composed of living things.
Livestock are biotic resources, composed of living things.
Rocks are abiotic resources, composed of non-living things.
Fisheries are biotic resources, composed of living things.

questions.explanation: Abiotic resources are composed of non-living things. Rocks, minerals, and metals fall under this category, while forests, livestock, and fisheries are biotic (living) resources.
questions.subject: icse10-sst

questions.question: Resources that can be renewed or reproduced by physical, chemical, or mechanical processes are known as:

options.explanation: Non-renewable resources are those that cannot be replenished over a period of time.
Individual resources are not a type of resource.
Renewable resources are those that can be replenished over a period of time.
Potential resources are those that are found in a region but have not been utilized.

questions.explanation: Renewable resources are those that can be replenished over a period of time, such as solar energy, wind energy, water, forests, and wildlife.

questions.question: The concept of 'Sustainable Development' primarily aims to:

options.text: Achieve economic growth at any cost.
options.explanation: Sustainable development prioritizes environmental protection and social equity over economic growth.
Sustainable development emphasizes long-term sustainability over short-term gains.

options.text: Develop without damaging the environment and compromising the needs of future generations.
options.explanation: Sustainable development aims to meet the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

options.text: Transfer resource ownership to international bodies.
options.explanation: Sustainable development does not involve transferring resource ownership to international bodies.

questions.explanation: Sustainable development emphasizes meeting the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, focusing on environmental protection and equitable development.

questions.question: Resources that are found in a region but have not been utilised are known as:

questions.question: In hilly regions, farmers often use techniques like contour ploughing and terrace farming. The primary objective behind these practices is to:

options.text: Control soil erosion caused by wind.

options.text: Reduce the speed of water flow and prevent soil erosion.

questions.explanation: Contour ploughing involves ploughing parallel to the contours of a hill slope, while terrace farming involves cutting steps on slopes.
